title: Physics 2: Electricity, Magnetism, Waves & Optics
subject: Electromagnetism
summary: Calculus-based electricity and magnetism from Coulomb to Maxwell, then mechanical waves, sound, geometric and wave optics. Prepares for Griffiths-level E&M and for quantum mechanics; chemistry hooks include molecular dipoles, dielectrics, the Hall effect and mass spectrometry, NMR magnetic moments, the EM spectrum, polarimetry and X-ray diffraction.

units.title: Electric Charge & Electric Field
units.summary: Coulomb's law, superposition, and the electric field of point charges, continuous distributions and dipoles; the dipole moment is the bridge to polar molecules and solvent behaviour.

lessons.title: Electric Charge & Coulomb's Law
objectives: State the properties of electric charge (quantisation, conservation, two signs) and classify materials as conductors or insulators.
Compute the Coulomb force between point charges as a vector and add several forces by superposition.
Compare the strengths of electric and gravitational forces between two protons and explain why electrostatics dominates chemistry.
Explain charging by induction and polarisation of a neutral object near a charge.

readings.title: Conductors, Insulators, and Charging by Induction

units.title: Gauss's Law
units.summary: Electric flux, Gauss's law, and its use for fields with spherical, cylindrical and planar symmetry; conductors in electrostatic equilibrium and shielding.

Explain why charge outside a closed surface contributes zero net flux.
